title: JustEnoughItems issue #4344: [Bug]: Flashback replays of servers can't be opened if JEI is installed
licence: GitHub issue thread: user-generated content under the GitHub Terms of Service; the repo licence (MIT) does not cover issue text
text: [issue by Syntrait] ### Steps to Reproduce the Bug 1. Join a Minecraft server 2. Start recording a Flashback replay 3. Return to the main menu 4. Try opening the replay file 5. Error when world is loading ### Expected Behavior I expected JEI to not error out the replay file ### Actual Behavior Replay file ends up not opening due to the error ### Mod Pack URL (Optional) _No response_ ### Mod Pack Version (Optional) _No response_ ### Extra Notes (Optional) Disabling JEI allows me to open the replay file in Flashback. Launching a singleplayer session's replay file does work even with JEI installed. Minecraft version: 1.21.11 JEI version: 27.4.0.24 Flashback version: 0.39.5 ### latest.log https://gist.github.com/Syntrait/d9fa592f4d43c7da7f239d31f05195f7 [comment by mezz (owner)] Thanks for the report! https://gist.github.com/Syntrait/1211ec0d44651fd6f9580c69720c9602 [comment by mezz (owner)] Thanks for narrowing things down. The issue here is still the same: > Failed to encode packet 'clientbound/minecraft:custom_payload' (fabric:recipe_sync) If you remove JEI, does that error still happen? [comment by mezz (owner)] It looks like something similar has been reported on Flashback's discord: https://discord.com/channels/1257203701349875753/1506633809716838480/1506633809716838480 But the author is very strict about the reports accepted, so we'll need a clear reproduction of this issue. While you do that, I will look into the Flashback code a bit. [comment by Syntrait (none)] Sounds good. The author of Flashback also mentioned to not ask for backports, and REI doesn't cause issues when installed alongside Flashback, so I thought it would be a good idea to make a bug report to JEI. After disabling JEI, the replay file did load in successfully. https://gist.github.com/Syntrait/28f6c33621fd02ca2bf2c45051be7002 [comment by mezz (owner)] Thanks for confirming, that narrows down the issue a bit more. JEI requests a recipe sync from Fabric, and REI has its own recipe sync mechanism so it doesn't make that request. I think that Flashback is doing something unusual that causes Fabric to trigger the recipe sync at a bad time, causing the crash. I will see if I can figure out if the issue is really caused by Flashback in my dev environment, and then discuss with the author. [comment by mezz (owner)] I tried to reproduce this myself, but wasn't able to. The issue may be from a specific replay. Can you try making a new recording with just JEI and then load that? [comment by Syntrait (none)] Did you record a singleplayer session? JEI does not cause issues for replays recorded in singleplayer. It only causes issues on replays recorded on multiplayer. P.S: I am now facing a new bug, this time JEI doesn't even work by itself https://github.com/mezz/JustEnoughItems/issues/4351, even though it was working a few hours ago. It says: "java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 0 out of bounds for length 0" [comment by mezz (owner)] I only tried a singleplayer session before, but now I tried a multiplayer recording. It still worked without any issues. I think there is something else that's required in order to replicate your bug. Can you please try starting from scratch with a new recording? [comment by Syntrait (none)] I am starting from scratch with a new recording, and it still happens. Here's a video of it, accompanied with the logs. Video: https://files.catbox.moe/837mxc.mp4 (github didn't let me upload for some reason) Logs: https://gist.github.com/Syntrait/d4627d2f6ca7668d1152de1c3ce6875b [comment by mezz (owner)] Ok thanks for the video. It looks like JEI is not installed on the server, which is why I couldn't reproduce the issue. I think the problem here is that the server environment is different from your local environment, I'll see if I can reproduce the issue. [comment by mezz (owner)] I was able to reproduce this issue by including owo-lib
